newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-MONTGOMERIE SEIZES LEAD IN EURO GRAND PRIX.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-MONTGOMERIE SEIZES LEAD IN EURO GRAND PRIX.

text.p: Colin Montgomerie set up his first European Tour victory chance of the season with a four-under-par 68 for a one-shot lead after the second round of the European Grand Prix on Friday.
Montgomerie's late decision to request an invitation to the event the week before the U.S. Open looks to have proved a wise one.
He climbed to seven-under with another exhilerating start to edge one shot ahead of the defending champion Retief Goosen of South Africa and fellow Briton Barry Lane.
Three more Britons are a further stroke back, Steven Bottomley, Paul Lawrie and David Carter, with Spaniard Ignacio Feliu.
First-round leader Steve Webster of England slumped to a 76 to fall five shots off the pace.
Three birdies in the first four holes got Montgomerie off to a flying start and he went into the lead by the fourth.
A stroke of luck when his ball struck hazard sleepers and bounced back into play on the awkward ninth kept his momentum and he moved one ahead of the field by picking up another shot on the 11th.

His first bogey since dropping a shot at the 15th hole in the third round of his previous event, the PGA Championship, came at the 13th when he misclubbed to go over the green, but the reigning European number one got back on course with a huge 40ft birdie putt on the 16th.
"I'm exactly where I feel most comfortable in Europe and that's on top of the leaderboard with everyone looking up at me," said Montgomerie.
"I came here to get into contention, especially bearing in mind it's the U.S. Open next week.
Goosen birdied the last two holes for a 69 to give himself hopes of back to back victories here.

"I obviously like the course but there are parts of my game where I'm struggling, having difficulty reading the lines on the greens, for instance. And my driving is not too good, but I can keep the ball in play with my irons," said the big-hitting South African.
Lane has had a poor start to his season but challenged Montgomerie with a good run in the middle of his opening nine holes, picking up an eagle and two birdies to go on to card 68 as well.
